commits.author: Marco Andronaco
commits.subject: feat: add jump-to-end buttons
commits.body:
Add jump-to-top/bottom buttons to both the chat and the sessions list,
shown once that end is more than 320px away. useJumpAffordances reads whichever
element actually scrolls, since the chat owns its scroller in desktop mode while
mobile lists scroll the page. Jumping to the top of a page-scrolled list has to
target the window: scrolling the list into view instead stranded the header
above the fold and left the button visible with nowhere to go.

commits.author: Marco Andronaco
commits.subject: fix: stop a lean history snapshot from swallowing sent messages
commits.body:
loadSelected rejected a fetched snapshot outright whenever it carried less
assistant text than was already on screen, to avoid erasing streamed output.
But the optimistic user bubble is cleared against that same snapshot either
way, so a just-sent message vanished the moment the server answered with a
leaner history. Worse, the rejected snapshot never reached state, so the
comparison stayed true and every later message was swallowed too, until the
session was reopened and the transcript reset.

Hold shrinking text back per part instead: same-id, same-type text and
reasoning parts keep the longer version, while the snapshot itself is always
applied. That keeps streamed output intact without ever dropping the messages
that arrived with it, and removes the need for the external-history escape
hatch, since a corrected external history now replaces the cache on its own.

Also restore the chat's bottom clearance on mobile, where the media query's
`padding: 0` shorthand was wiping the padding-bottom that reserves room for
the sticky composer.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: fix: stop the empty chat pane from claiming it is loading
commits.body:
With no session selected, the conversation pane sat on "Loading session…"
forever. Both of its load checks compare a value against selectedID, so
a null selectedID satisfied `loadingSessionID === selectedID` and the
spinner never resolved — there was nothing to wait for.

Mobile never showed it: the Detail tab is disabled until a session is
picked. The desktop layout renders the pane unconditionally beside the
sidebar, so anyone connecting to a server with no sessions yet, or
closing Settings before picking one, met a spinner that would not stop.

Nothing selected is its own state, so it now gets its own branch ahead of
the load checks, reusing the "Select a session" string the header already
shows. The remaining checks only run once there is a session, which is
what they were written to describe.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: docs: document desktop mode in the README and the Help page
commits.body:
The app has had two layouts since desktop mode landed and nothing said so.
The README described bottom navigation only, leaving the sidebar, the
draggable panel borders and the persisted widths to be found by accident,
and the Help page told a desktop reader to open sessions from a tab that
is not on their screen.

The README gets a Desktop Mode section: where the 781px boundary is, what
changes across it, and the five things needed to actually drive it. The
Help page's Overview now describes whichever layout is currently rendered
and names the boundary, so a window dragged past it reads as a layout
change rather than a lost sidebar. The breakpoint becomes a constant,
since quoting it to the user made a third copy of the literal.

CONTRIBUTING gains the layout counterpart to the two-backends rule. Both
traps are already load-bearing in the code: the scroller changes identity
across the breakpoint, and the session card is rendered twice from one
function. Its "where to start" also stopped pointing at issue #36, which
shipped as PI support in v2.2.0.
